# Turn on notifications
{: .no_toc }

Explain, request the OS permission, and register this install for push.
{: .fs-6 .fw-300 }

| | |
|---|---|
| **Screen ID** | `NTF-04` |
| **Route** | `/account/devices/enable` · deep link `substratal://account/devices/enable` |
| **Where** | Personal › Account |
| **Who can use it** | Self |
| **Kind** | wizard |
| **Available in** | All Hub apps (Phase 2) |
| **On Linux** | `AdwDialog` with `AdwNavigationView` pages |

**How you get here:** First time a notification-worthy moment happens (org invite, first launch after sign-in on mobile, enabling in NTF-03/SET-01) — never on cold start before sign-in

## What's on this screen

| Element | What it is | Shows / does | Rules | On Linux |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Primer | text + illustration |  | what you'll get: security alerts, invitations, access changes; "You can change this anytime" | GtkLabel |
| Turn on | primary-button | OS permission prompt | platform API per PLATFORM-SPEC | GtkButton .suggested-action .pill |
| Not now | button |  | snooze 14 days | GtkButton |

## What happens when you act

| Action | API call | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Permission granted | `POST /users/me/devices {application_id: app_hub, provider, token \` | subscription, environment (apns), name, app_version}` |
| Token rotated by OS | `PATCH /users/me/devices/{deviceId} {token \` | subscription}` |
| Permission denied | `—` | Settings shows "Blocked — Open system settings" deep link |

## Good to know

- Re-register on launch at most once a day (keeps the device from going stale after 270 days). Windows and Linux have no supported push provider in the API: this screen is replaced by an in-app explanation and local notifications from polling (see their PLATFORM-SPEC).
